description: A feature flag in the load generator's `locustfile.py` activated a `flood_home` Locust task (weighted 5/32, ~16% of selection per cycle) that fired `flood_count = 100` rapid GETs to the frontend homepage; outbound HTTP request rate from the load generator spiked, driving container CPU and network traffic on the frontend and frontend-proxy containers above baseline.
mechanism:
The flag is read in [`locustfile.py#L220`](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/load-generator/locustfile.py#L220), inside the load generator's Locust test suite.

Each simulated user repeats this loop:

1. Execute one randomly-chosen task (weighted)
2. Wait for `wait_time` (1–10 seconds, [line 114](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/load-generator/locustfile.py#L114))
3. Go back to step 1

One iteration of that loop is a "cycle." Each user runs independently and concurrently. There are **5 simulated users** (see [`.env#L101`](../../opentelemetry-demo/.env#L101)).

`flood_home` has a **5/32 (~16%) chance** of being selected each cycle. When selected, it sends `flood_count` rapid requests to the homepage. The `flood_count` value is **100**, defined in [`demo.flagd.json#L105`](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/flagd/demo.flagd.json#L105).

variants.description: Network bytes received by the load-generator container increased ~1.5-2.5x (from ~28,500 B/s to 46,000-71,000 B/s) as it ingested homepage responses from the 100-request flood bursts
variants.onset_reasoning: Pre-incident baseline is ~28,200-28,750. At 15:00 the value jumps to 29,750, exceeding the baseline maximum by ~1,000, and continues rising sharply to 35,104 at 15:01 and beyond. 15:00 is the first clear departure above baseline.

variants.description: Network bytes transmitted by the load-generator container increased ~1.2-1.5x (from ~12,800 B/s to 15,500-19,000 B/s) as it sent the flood of homepage GET requests to frontend-proxy
variants.onset_reasoning: Pre-incident baseline hovers around 12,700-13,075. At 15:01 the value jumps to 13,853, clearly breaking above the baseline ceiling, and continues rising sharply to 16,000+ in subsequent minutes.

variants.description: Network bytes received by the frontend-proxy container surged ~25-50x (from ~900 B/s to 21,000-49,000 B/s) because the load generator's flood_home task sent 100 rapid homepage GET requests per invocation through the Envoy proxy
variants.onset_reasoning: Pre-incident baseline fluctuates roughly 760-1060 bytes/s. At 15:00 UTC (one minute after the incident marker), the value jumps to ~2472, already well above the baseline range, and continues climbing rapidly to ~30k+. This is the first clear departure from the baseline.

variants.description: Network bytes received by the frontend container increased ~4-5x (from ~700 B/s to 3,000-5,700 B/s) as the frontend-proxy forwarded the flood of homepage requests to the Next.js frontend
variants.onset_reasoning: Pre-incident baseline fluctuates roughly 550-880 bytes/s. At 15:00 (one minute after incident at 14:59:28), the value jumps to 870 and then rapidly escalates to 1583, 2419, 3350+ in subsequent minutes, never returning to baseline. 15:00 marks the start of this sustained exponential rise.

variants.description: Jaeger bulk index attempts tripled as the storage layer processed more batches of spans from the flood-induced traffic surge
variants.onset_reasoning: Pre-incident baseline fluctuates roughly between 6-20. At 15:00 the value (14.29) is still within normal range. At 15:01 it jumps to 27.63, clearly exceeding the pre-incident maximum of ~20.8, marking the start of the sustained spike to 50-67 levels.

logs.name: load-generator: User flooding homepage 100 times (INFO)
logs.description: Starting at 14:59:41.379 UTC and continuing through 15:09:28.578 UTC, load-generator emitted 34 flood_home logs confirming loadGeneratorFloodHomepage is ON with value 100. The downstream effect is visible in frontend-proxy Envoy access logs as a surge in homepage GETs starting at 14:59 UTC (baseline ~1-3 req/min through 14:58, climbing to 100-561 req/min during 14:59-15:09), all returning HTTP 200.
logs.cause: Direct effect of the loadGeneratorFloodHomepage feature flag. When flagd returns a value > 0, locust's flood_home task starts a user_flood_home span (attribute flood.count=100) and logs 'User flooding homepage {flood_count} times' before issuing that many GET / requests against frontend-proxy.
